verdict.rationale: Buzz is built on an open Nostr relay protocol that third-party clients can use directly. Its CLI and agent skill cover a broad range of operations: messaging, channels, DMs, workflows, canvas, repos, uploads and branch protection. Agents are documented doing repos, patches, reviews, workflows, canvases and huddles, so programmatic coverage is extensive, but no source explicitly guarantees full UI parity, and the OpenAPI probe found no published REST spec. Missing for 10: an explicit documented UI/API parity guarantee, a published REST/OpenAPI reference, evidence for UI-only features like frame-anchored video comments and personalized feed via API, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: open repos, send patches, review code, run workflows, edit canvases, orchestrate other agents, drop into voice huddles, create channels
Third-party Nostr clients connect directly to `buzz-relay` using NIP-29 and NIP-42 authentication.
relay operations: owner-reviewed agent drafts, messaging, channels, DMs, users, workflows, feed, reactions, canvas, social, repos, uploads, and agent memory.
